title: VPC operator evacuation and cutover checklist
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Purpose
This document is an operator-focused checklist and procedural guide for evacuating VPC tenants and performing controlled cutovers during regional network failures, severe interconnect degradation, or cloud provider maintenance windows. It complements the existing safe-failover playbooks and provides concrete commands, verification steps, and escalation paths for on-call and field operators.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood Private VPC deployments (customer-managed networks and Redwood-managed control plane) where tenant compute or data plane needs planned or emergent redirection.
- Covers three evacuation modes: graceful drain, accelerated swap, and emergency quarantine.
- Excludes airgap/airgapped on-prem appliance procedures (see onprem-packaging runbooks).

Summary of evacuation modes
1) Graceful drain: Move traffic off a zone/region with >60 minutes lead time. Preserve KV cache checkpoints, warm workers, and allow in-flight requests to complete. Best for planned maint windows.
2) Accelerated swap: Short lead (<60 min) redirect using regional routing policies and cached model fallbacks. Prioritizes availability over cost.
3) Emergency quarantine: Immediate isolation of suspected tenant compromise or catastrophic network partition. Operator must snapshot telemetry and preserve evidence before state mutation.

Ownership and roles
- Primary operator: field operator on duty (first responder for execution).
- Oncall SRE: validates telemetry and approves regional policy flips.
- Solutions owner (customer success): notified for customer-facing communication.
- Incident commander: owns communication cadence and cross-team escalations.

Pre-evacuation checklist (must complete before any action)
- Confirm active incident or scheduled maintenance in status dashboard and Slack #ops.
- Validate recent model binary and quantization compatibility: run quick artifact compatibility check (see artifact-check command below).
- Ensure at least one healthy fallback region with compatible models and sufficient reserved capacity. Target: 120% of projected peak for next 2 hours.
- Snapshot KV cache checkpoint: run redwoodctl kv checkpoint --tenant <TENANT_ID> --preserve-metadata.
- Lock rollout gates: set rollout_lock=true in the tenant policy to prevent model swaps during eviction.

Quick artifact compatibility check (example)
- Command: 
  redwoodctl artifact verify --tenant $TENANT --model $MODEL_ID --quant $PROFILE
- Expected output: 
  {
    "status": "ok",
    "backward_compatible": true,
    "missing_kernels": []
  }

Evacuation procedures
A. Graceful drain (planned maintenance)
1. Notify stakeholders (customer success, security, infra) and create temporary status page entry.
2. Scale target fallback region up by +25% capacity: redwoodctl scale --region $FALLBACK --pool reserved --pct 125
3. Start KV checkpoint and confirm TTLs: redwoodctl kv checkpoint --tenant $T --wait 300
4. Initiate routing slow drain (traffic shift 5% every 2 minutes) via routing policy:
   curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/shift -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"tenant":"'$T'","from":"us-east-1","to":"us-west-2","step_pct":5,"step_interval_s":120}'
5. Monitor tail latency and 95th percentile token latency; abort if 95p latency exceeds 2x baseline for >3 windows.
6. When traffic <5% on source, cordon nodes and drain workloads with graceful timeout 300s: kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --timeout=300s --ignore-daemonsets
7. After drain, snapshot runtime logs and mark change in incident timeline.

B. Accelerated swap (short lead)
1. Validate fallback capacity and model compatibility (quick artifact check).
2. Enable accelerated routing policy: set step_pct=25 and step_interval_s=60.
3. Pre-warm model caches in fallback region using synthetic prefixes and representative prompt sets: redwoodctl warm --tenant $T --model $MODEL --qps 50 --duration 120
4. Execute swap and run verification job (see Verification section). If verification fails, automatic rollback policy will revert after 5 minutes unless operator manually extends.

C. Emergency quarantine (compromise or total partition)
1. Immediately snapshot telemetry and operator evidence: redwoodctl telemetry export --tenant $T --since "1h" --output /tmp/$T-evidence.tar.gz
2. Apply network-policy deny-all for tenant: kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-quarantine
  namespace: tenant-$T
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  - Ingress
  ingress: []
  egress: []
EOF
3. Mark incident as security-sensitive and contact security@redwood.com and legal if customer data exposure risk > medium.
4. Run forensic snapshot of model artifacts and control-plane audit logs. Do NOT mutate model artifacts until forensic review completes.

Verification and acceptance tests
- Post-cutover verification (automated):
  - healthcheck: /internal/health returns 200 for all endpoints
  - sample inference suite (10 representative prompts) latency < baseline * 1.5 and correctness pass rate >= 98% (per tenant eval set)
  - KV checkpoint integrity: key-count delta <= 0.5%
- Manual checks: survey the QPS distribution, watch for queue buildup, confirm that rate-limiters are functioning.

Monitoring thresholds and SLOs
- Availability SLO for cutover window: 99.5% (target) measured as successful inference responses / total requests in the 30-minute window post-cutover.
- Target alert thresholds:
  - 95p token latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> P1 alert to oncall and SRE.
  - Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 5 minutes -> P1.
  - KV cache miss rate > 10% for 10 minutes -> P2 (operator investigation).

Rollback policy and criteria
- Automatic rollback triggers (system will revert if any condition persists >5 minutes):
  - 95p token latency > 3x baseline, or
  - Error rate increase > 1.5% absolute, or
  - Model compatibility failure reported by artifact verifier.
- Manual rollback steps:
  1. Pause routing policy (set step_pct=0).
  2. Revert traffic to source region using controlplane API: curl -X POST /routing/policies/revert ...
  3. Restore KV checkpoint (if necessary): redwoodctl kv restore --tenant $T --checkpoint /snapshots/$T-<ts>.tar.gz --force
  4. Re-open nodes for traffic after validation.

Post-evacuation tasks and evidence
- Create incident timeline with timestamps for each major action and attach KV checkpoint IDs and telemetry bundles.
- Run a targeted postmortem if any P1/P0 conditions were observed.
- Add lessoned learned to the tenant-runbook and mark the tenant policy with updated evacuation window if needed.

Configuration matrix (reference)
|| Item || Recommended value || Notes ||
|| Fallback over-provisioning || 120–150% || Depends on historical burst patterns ||
|| KV checkpoint frequency || Every 30 minutes during window || Decrease frequency during high-cost windows ||
|| Model warm qps || 20–100 || Use representative prompt set; avoid training-like workloads ||
|| Rollout safety gates || 95p latency, error-rate, kv-integrity || All must be green to proceed beyond 50% traffic shift ||

Common operator troubleshooting commands
- Check routing policy status: curl -s https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/$POLICY | jq
- Inspect node drain status: kubectl get pods -n tenant-$T -o wide --field-selector status.phase!=Running
- Tail inference logs for tenant: kubectl logs -n tenant-$T -l app=inference -f --since=10m
- Reapply kv checkpoint: redwoodctl kv restore --tenant $T --checkpoint $CP_ID

Communication templates (quick)
- Customer-facing (short): 
  Subject: Planned maintenance affecting inference latency for <TENANT>
  Body: We will be performing a controlled traffic cutover from region A to region B at <TIME>. We expect a brief period of elevated latency for up to 30 minutes; expected availability is >99.5%. We will notify you when the operation completes.

- Internal escalation (Slack):
  @oncall-sre P1: initiating accelerated swap for <TENANT>. Fallback region: $REGION. Monitoring: #telemetry. Rolling back if 95p latency > 3x baseline for >5m.

Runbook maintenance and links
- Owner: Marisol Chen (eng-private-deployments)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P1/P0 evacuation.
- Related: tenant eviction playbook, control plane routing API reference, artifact compatibility guide.

Appendix: sample accelerated routing JSON payload
{
  "tenant": "tenant-12345",
  "from": "eu-west-1",
  "to": "eu-central-1",
  "mode": "accelerated",
  "step_pct": 25,
  "step_interval_s": 60,
  "safety_gates": {"95p_latency_multiplier": 2.0, "error_rate_delta": 0.005, "kv_integrity_delta": 0.01},
  "auto_rollback_minutes": 5
}

If you find gaps or run into edge cases not covered here, please open an RFC in the eng-private-deployments space and tag the owner.
